facts.fact: UNICEF Mali states that under the PAIS project each family in the target areas holds an electronic card with each child registered on it, which the school principal scans onto a tablet as children attend, to take attendance and make it available to the Ministry of Education; upload is possible at least once a month at Kénèkolo; no date is given beyond '2020', so the published month is used.
facts.system: PAIS electronic family card and tablet attendance

facts.fact: UNICEF Mali gives no count or share of schools scanning attendance: it says families in the target areas of Kayes, Koulikoro, Ségou and Sikasso have been given cards and that the Kénèkolo school 'will digitize' its attendance system in 2020; it does not call the scheme a pilot.
facts.system: PAIS electronic family card and tablet attendance

facts.fact: UNICEF Mali describes the scheme at the Kénèkolo village school, in a passage on children aged seven to twelve missing primary education; the survey behind the cards covers children aged 6 to 15, and the article names no school level outright.
facts.system: PAIS electronic family card and tablet attendance

facts.fact: UNICEF Mali states that PAIS is a partnership of UNICEF, the World Food Programme, the International Rescue Committee and the Norwegian Refugee Council, with the household survey devised and run by the local company VooLinks; the ministry is named only as a recipient of the data.
facts.system: PAIS electronic family card and tablet attendance

facts.fact: UNICEF Mali states that the PAIS project is funded by the European Union and aims to return 250,000 children to school by 2022.
facts.system: PAIS electronic family card and tablet attendance

systems.system: PAIS electronic family card and tablet attendance
systems.platform: electronic card scanned on a tablet
systems.owner: UNICEF with WFP, IRC and NRC; survey by VooLinks; funded by the European Union
systems.tiers: school: the principal scans each family's card as children attend and uploads when a connection allows; target areas in Kayes, Koulikoro, Ségou and Sikasso

note: Classed emis on what the article says it does: a per-child attendance record added at the school during the year and sent to the ministry. The article mixes present and future tense on whether scanning had begun at Kénèkolo.
